references.text: The angel of the Lord appears in the burning bush and calls to Moses, who continues the narrative from verse 2.
The angel of the Lord (מַלְאַךְ יְהֹוָה) appears to Hagar, showing a similar pattern of divine revelation.
The angel of the Lord calls out to Abraham from heaven, another example of the angel of the Lord conveying God's message.
God reveals Himself in fire (the pillar of fire) to lead Israel, connecting the theme of God's presence in fire.
Moses blesses Joseph and mentions 'He who dwelt in the bush' (שֹׁכְנִי סְנֶה), a direct reference to this revelation.
The angel of the Lord appears to Balaam, another example of divine revelation through the angel of the Lord.
The angel of the Lord appears to Gideon with fire rising from the rock, similar to the theophany of fire.
Isaiah's vision of the glory of the Lord with seraphim and fire, showing God's holy presence revealed in fire.
Stephen quotes this event in his speech and mentions the angel who appeared in the flame of fire in the bush.
Jesus refers to 'the passage about the burning bush' when He speaks of the resurrection and calls God 'the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob'.
Jesus refers to Moses at the burning bush when He argues for the resurrection from the dead.
Describes God as a consuming fire, connecting the theme of God's holy presence revealed in fire.
The same historical event confirmed in New Testament explanation.
Direct allusion linking Moses' call to the angel in the bush.
